items.title: Sick of Constant Pings, They’re Sending Texts at the Speed of Carrier Pigeon
items.author: Emmett Lindner
items.content: <article>Apps that let users send digital messages at ultraslow speeds have taken off, with users reveling in a slower pace of life. (Just don’t use the them to make dinner plans.)</article>

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Buys an Irish Castle
items.author: Alan Yuhas
items.content: <article>The prominent landowner has added a nearly 200-year-old estate to his holdings. Archival information says it can take “a brisk walk of 4½ minutes to reach the dining room from the kitchen.”</article>

items.title: Apollo’s Slok Says AI Weighs On Pay Without Cutting Jobs — Yet
items.author: David Westin
items.content: <article>Torsten Slok found something surprising when Apollo Global Management Inc. looked at how the adoption of artificial intelligence was playing out in the labor market.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Could Aim to Raise $100 Billion in Blockbuster I.P.O.
items.author: Sri Muppidi, Lauren Hirsch and Erin Griffith
items.content: <article>The offering could value the five-year-old A.I. start-up at $2 trillion, its bankers have told potential investors, which would exceed Elon Musk’s SpaceX.</article>

items.title: ITG CFO: We're the Picks & Shovels of the AI Boom
items.content: <article>Chris Mecray, CFO at ITG, joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the company's performance since its July 1 IPO, and its role in the AI buildout as a fiber and communications company. Mecray says ITG is "the picks and shovels of the AI boom... with a long runway of opportunity associated with creating the connectivity that data centers require once the actual site itself is built." Mecray speaks with Carol Massar, Emily Graffeo, and Nina Trentmann, CFO Briefing Editor. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: TikTok Settles With U.S. Over Child Privacy Concerns for $400 Million
items.author: David McCabe
items.content: <article>The Justice Department resolved a lawsuit that accused the social media company of illegally gathering children’s information.</article>

items.title: Stocks Rally but End a Volatile Week Lower | The Close 8/21/2026
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are ProShares Head of Research & Active Investments CIO Alessio de Longis, KPMG Chief Economist Diane Swonk, Goldman Sachs Co-Head, Global Commodities Research Daan Struyven, Janus Henderson Portfolio Manager Jeremiah Buckley, National Academy of Engineering President Tsu-Jae King Liu, Loop CEO Matt McKinney, Liquid Death Founder & CEO Mike Cessario, Legendary Sports Agent Leigh Steinberg, & Boxer Mike Tyson. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Liquid Death CEO on Viral AI Data Center Ad, IPO Odds
items.content: <article>Mike Cessario, Founder and CEO of Liquid Death, joined the program to discuss the growing public sentiment against the rapid expansion of data centers. Despite widespread interest in AI investments, the mood around data center growth has been notably negative. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Chip Engineer Tsu-Jae King Liu on Nvidia, AI Energy Need
items.content: <article>Doctor Tsu-Jae King Liu, President of the National Academy of Engineering and Former Dean of UC Berkeley's College of Engineering, joined the program to discuss her influential role in the semiconductor industry. Having served on the board of Intel and contributed to the design of chips found in mobile phones, she shared insights into the technological advancements and impact of semiconductors in everyday devices. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Swonk: Fed Independence, Inflation Key for Jackson Hole
items.content: <article>Diane Swonk, KPMG Chief Economist, discusses expectations for the upcoming Federal Reserve speech at the Jackson Hole Economic Symposium. The speech is traditionally technical and focused on internal task forces, but markets are seeking clearer guidance on inflation and monetary policy. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: In China’s Biggest Car Recall, Tesla and 8 Others Will Address Door Safety
items.author: Keith Bradsher and Jack Ewing
items.content: <article>China’s regulator ordered changes after vehicle occupants sometimes had difficulty exiting electric cars, an issue that has led to lawsuits against Tesla in the United States.</article>

items.title: TikTok to Pay $400 Million to Settle DOJ Child Privacy Case
items.author: Josh Sisco and Alexandra S. Levine
items.content: <article>TikTok Inc. and Chinese parent ByteDance Ltd. agreed to pay $400 million to resolve a a Biden-era lawsuit by the Justice Department accusing the popular social media app of collecting data on children in violation of an online privacy law.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Taps Google Chip Veteran as Part of Push Into Hardware
items.author: Dina Bass
items.content: <article>Anthropic PBC has hired Amir Salek, a founder of the custom chip program at Alphabet Inc.’s Google, as the AI lab lays the groundwork for a push into making its own semiconductors.</article>

items.title: Ask Emily Chang About Interviewing Tech’s Biggest Names on The Circuit
items.author: Emily Chang and Brad Stone
items.content: Emily Chang interviews the top names in tech and business on The Circuit. Bring your questions and join her for an interactive Live Q&A conversation on Sept. 1 at 1 p.m. EDT

items.title: SpaceX Is Hiring in Natural Gas Trading for Energy Needs
items.author: Julian Hast
items.content: <article>Elon Musk’s SpaceX is hiring a trader to build and lead a natural gas trading team to support the space flight company’s growing fuel and power needs.</article>

items.title: Treasury Whiplash, US Debt Hits $40T | Bloomberg Money 8/21/2026
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Rebecca Patterson, Council on Foreign Relations Senior Fellow, and Kevin Gordon, Charles Schwab Head of Macro Research & Strategy. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Khosla Ventures Bets on AI’s Next Frontier: Science
items.content: <article>Khosla Ventures is backing Discovery Loop, a new AI startup founded by former Google leaders including Jeff Dean that aims to dramatically accelerate scientific experimentation. Khosla Ventures Managing Director Samir Kaul explains why the firm quickly decided to invest, and why he believes the opportunity could be as profound as frontier AI models. He also discusses why soaring technology valuations are forcing venture investors to rethink what “seed stage” even means. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Meta Safety Trial Could Reveal What Zuckerberg, Others Knew
items.content: <article>Meta is facing a landmark legal battle with 29 states accusing the company of deliberately designing its platforms to keep children hooked while misleading the public about their safety. George Washington University law professor Mary Anne Franks explains the state and federal claims, why the case has drawn comparisons to tobacco litigation, and why the biggest consequence may not be the potential financial penalty, but what internal documents reveal about what Meta knew and when. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Wall Street Struggles to Absorb AI’s Debt Boom
items.content: <article>Broadcom is lining up another massive bet on AI. Bloomberg has learned the chipmaker is in talks to raise more than $60 billion in debt to help Anthropic and others secure chips and computing power. The deal highlights a bigger concern hanging over the AI trade: the cost of funding it all. Erica Klauer, Science and Technology Partners founder and CIO, discusses concerns around circular financing and why the AI buildout is so challenging. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Anthropic Preps for Blockbuster Public Listing | Bloomberg Tech 8/21/2026
items.content: <article>Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow takes a look at Anthropic as the AI company expects to match or top the size of SpaceX's record-setting IPO. Plus, sources say Broadcom is in talks to raise more than $60 billion in debt to help Anthropic and others secure chips and computing power, and all eyes are on Nvidia as the chipmaker reports earnings next week. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Anthropic Aims to Match or Top SpaceX IPO
items.content: <article>Anthropic is aiming for an IPO that could make history, expecting to match or even top SpaceX's record-setting debut, according to sources. The maker of Claude could file publicly by the end of this month. The company raised $65 billion in May at a $965 billion valuation. Bloomberg's Shirin Ghaffary, who leads coverage of Anthropic, and Bloomberg's Liana Baker, who leads the deals team, join Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Robinhood's Guild on AI, Markets & Risks
items.content: <article>Robinhood's Stephanie Guild discusses the impact of major AI IPOs, market concentration risks, opportunities in healthcare and compute infrastructure, and why investors should balance AI exposure with cash flow-focused, defensive assets. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Apple Cuts Jobs in Siri, Vision Pro Immersive Video and Gaming Teams
items.author: Mark Gurman
items.content: <article>Apple Inc. is cutting jobs across teams responsible for the Siri digital assistant and the Vision Pro headset, part of an effort to focus on new devices and artificial intelligence.</article>

items.title: Rockstar Rattled As ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Leaks Again
items.author: Jason Schreier
items.content: <article>After a leak in 2022 Rockstar took drastic measures to try to prevent another hack. It didn’t work.</article>

items.title: Voters Aren’t Waiting for November to Try Ousting Officials Over Data Centers
items.author: David McCabe
items.content: <article>As a backlash grows over data centers, more local officials are facing recall elections for their support of the computing sites.</article>

items.title: New Jersey Teenager Drops Bellwether Social Media Addiction Lawsuit
items.author: Eli Tan
items.content: <article>The case was the third of nine major personal injury cases that could expose Meta, YouTube, Snap and TikTok to financial damages and force them to change the designs of their platforms.</article>

items.title: AI Slop Is Everywhere. Spotify, LinkedIn and Others Have Had Enough.
items.author: Tiffany Hsu
items.content: <article>Spotify, LinkedIn and others are trying to dig out of a digital sewage heap full of low-quality content made with artificial intelligence.</article>

items.title: A County Got Rich From Data Centers. Some Question ‘At What Cost?’
items.author: Cecilia Kang and Caroline Gutman
items.content: <article>Loudoun County, Va., hosts more than 250 data centers that bring in huge tax revenues. But some officials and residents worry the county has become too dependent on that cash.</article>

items.title: OpenAI’s Two-Week Pause + Jill Lepore on the Threat of the “Artificial State” + Train of Thought
items.author: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Whitney Jones, Rachel Cohn, Vjeran Pavic, Katie McMurran, Dan Powell, Marion Lozano, Rowan Niemisto and Alyssa Moxley
items.content: <article>“It is the first time that we know of that a major lab has voluntarily slowed down.”</article>

items.title: Flock Cameras. Canoodling Lawyers. How Much Surveillance Are We Comfortable With?
items.author: Willy Staley
items.content: <article>Americans say they hate prying cameras. But they can’t look away.</article>

items.title: Nvidia to Pay AI Startup Poolside a $6 Billion License, Newcomer Says
items.author: Benoit Berthelot, Rebecca Torrence and Ian King
items.content: <article>Nvidia Corp. has agreed to pay $6 billion to license artificial intelligence models from Poolside and will extend job offers to more than 100 employees, according to people familiar with the situation.</article>

items.title: Two Binance Employees Detained in the U.A.E. Amid Police Inquiries
items.author: David Yaffe-Bellany and Michael Forsythe
items.content: <article>The detentions of the workers, who have been released, are a sign of legal pressure that the world’s largest crypto exchange faces in the Emirates, which is home to its main regulator.</article>

items.title: The Funny Way That Stand-Up Comics Are Posting on Social Media
items.author: Sopan Deb
items.content: <article>Comedians used to post footage of their performances to build a following. Now, some are finding that comic strip-style panels with captions pack a bigger punch.</article>

items.title: Chinese Start-Up Lands Reusable Rocket for the First Time
items.author: Adeel Hassan
items.content: <article>The milestone by the private company, LandSpace, could put China closer to challenging SpaceX’s rule in lower-cost spaceflight.</article>

items.title: Google’s Pixel 11 Comes With Plenty of A.I. Does Anyone Want That?
items.author: Brian X. Chen and Minh Connors
items.content: <article>The phone’s artificial intelligence can order groceries, book tables and take photos on a user’s behalf. But is it something people really want?</article>

items.title: Apple Removes Some Fees for App Developers in European Union
items.author: Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>The move followed a long battle with regulators over the company’s tight controls of its App Store.</article>

items.title: Meta to Stand Trial Over Claims It Addicted Children to Social Media
items.author: Cecilia Kang, Eli Tan and Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey have taken the social media giant to trial in the first bellwether federal case over child harm.</article>

items.title: Silicon Valley Executives Are Tech Fans. Just Not For Their Own Kids.
items.author: David Streitfeld
items.content: <article>At home, moderation and restraint are the rule for tech parents. Boredom is exalted. Maybe they’re onto something.</article>

items.title: ICE Bars Its Workers From Wearing Meta’s Smart Glasses on the Job
items.author: Eli Tan and Hamed Aleaziz
items.content: <article>The agency joins a growing number of workplaces and groups to ban Meta’s devices, which have spurred privacy concerns.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Introduces ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ as Safety Concerns Grow
items.author: Cecilia Kang
items.content: <article>The artificial intelligence start-up announced a chatbot mode that will automatically limit some conversations to better protect young users.</article>

items.title: The Blackout That Could Devastate America
items.author: Christopher Cox
items.content: <article>The power grid relies on thousands of aging, hand-built transformers. If enough fail, the blackout could last years.</article>

items.title: Nvidia to Back Ohio Data Center With as Much as $105 Billion
items.author: Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>The data center, one of the world’s largest, could cost as much as $500 billion and will be leased by OpenAI.</article>
